previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with end-stage renal disease, type 1 diabetes, and a history of bilateral lower extremity amputations was admitted for nausea and vomiting after taking Nyquil, along with a new nonproductive cough. She was found to have leukocytosis and a positive blood culture for Staphylococcus epidermidis, prompting evaluation for bacteremia. A tunneled hemodialysis catheter was lost on hospital day two, requiring temporary peritoneal dialysis, which she did not tolerate. After 24 hours of negative blood cultures, a new tunneled catheter was placed, and IV vancomycin was resumed. Infectious disease recommended a two-week course of vancomycin despite the likely contaminant, and transesophageal echocardiogram ruled out endocarditis. Urine culture grew E. coli, but due to lack of symptoms, it was deemed colonization and not treated. Her cough improved with bronchodilators and resolved by discharge. She was discharged home with services to complete vancomycin during dialysis and follow up with her care team.

# Health Care Associated Pneumonia: Patient presented with 
yellow productive cough associated with SOB, tachycardia, WBC 19 
with CXR showing right upper and possibly right lower lobe 
pneumonia. Patient was already on vancomycin for staph 
epidermidis bacteremia from prior hospitalization few days ago.  
She was started on Zosyn for HCAP coverage.  Her WBC continued 
to trend down from 19 to 9 in two days.  She remained afebrile 
with normal heart rate, her shortness of breath along with her 
cough improved substantially.  Per recommendation of ID team, 
she was switched from Zosyn to Levofloxacin for HCAP coverage 
prior to discharge. On the day of discharge patient was satting 
97% on room air and tolerating POs without any nausea or 
vomiting.  She will follow up with PCP for further care.
.

catheter.  There was no drainage or tracking along HD line.
